title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: voice recognition set in device settings instead of PowerShell
summary: Hold: the role guidance omits Microsoft's restriction on administrative-unit assignments, which cannot access the Pro Management portal. The rationales also incorrectly imply that rooms cannot identify speakers without the new device setting, although the briefing correctly documents the still-working meeting policy route.

claims.claim: The portal path is Rooms > Settings > Recognition > Configure with device settings.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The new Android settings replace the requirement to use PowerShell with a UI and clearer recognition-status visibility across rooms.
claims.quote: we're introducing new admin-facing settings on Android Teams Rooms devices. These settings replace PowerShell-based configuration with a more intuitive UI, offering clearer visibility into recognition status across rooms.

claims.claim: The recognition setting concerns speaker identification rather than an autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: Recognition data is used only for in-meeting identification, transcription, and AI-generated recaps.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the device settings route will remain once the meeting policy option is retired.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms roomAttributeUserOverride retirement Configure with device settings. Read people-recognition, pro-portal-settings and release notes; Microsoft recommends device settings and announces policy retirement, but does not state the post-retirement design.
claims.fix: Remove 'and it is the route Microsoft says will remain once the meeting policy option is retired' from Why it matters. The already-present statement that Microsoft recommends device settings is supported.

claims.claim: No room identifies enrolled speakers, and participants notice recognition only, after an administrator enables it through the new device setting.
claims.quote: risk: 'no room identifies enrolled people by voice until an admin turns it on for that device.' What's changing: 'The older route, the roomAttributeUserOverride parameter of the Teams meeting policy, still works'.
claims.fix: Replace the risk rationale with 'Low. The new Voice Recognition device setting is Off by default; Microsoft still documents the existing meeting policy configuration route.' Replace the impact rationale with 'Low. Room administrators see the new settings; enrolled meeting participants can notice speaker attribution in rooms configured for recognition.'

claims.claim: roomAttributeUserOverride accepts Off, Attribute or Distinguish.
claims.quote: -RoomAttributeUserOverride: Possible values: Off; Distinguish; Attribute
